chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from a group of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
A community is not sanctified unless the right of its weak is taken from its strong without hesitation.
ai.seo_question: What is the condition for a community to be considered sanctified according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this concise narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), linking communal sanctity (quds) directly to the equitable enforcement of rights (huquq) for the vulnerable. The term 'ghayra muta'ta'in' (without hesitation or stuttering) underscores the immediacy and decisiveness required in social justice, reflecting the Shia emphasis on active, rather than passive, righteousness. This hadith serves as a foundational principle for the concept of 'Amr bil-Ma'ruf wa Nahi anil-Munkar', illustrating that true holiness is manifested through the protection of the weak from the oppression of the strong.
